Pratap Maurya @ Ram Pratap vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy.
Home Lko. on 12 March, 2024

Author: Pankaj Bhatia
Bench: Pankaj Bhatia
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:22098
Court No. - 12
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 12072 of 2023
Applicant :- Pratap Maurya @ Ram Pratap

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy.
Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Divya Prakash,Mohd. Shahid Akhtar,Pankaj Kumar Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.270 of 2017, under Sections 498A, 304B, 302 IPC & Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S.- Khairabad, District-Sitapur.
3. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the sister of the informant was married to the applicant in the year 2017 and subsequently, she was killed by the entire matrimonial family.
This is the fourth bail application.

The first bail application filed by the applicant was rejected on 26.02.2020,
however, directions were issued for concluding the trial within one year, the second bail application Pratap Maurya @ Ram Pratap vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Pratap Maurya @ Ram Pratap vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko

sentences.text:

1 was rejected on 16.05.2022 for non-prosecution.
The third bail application was rejected vide order dated 20.09.2022 with directions to expedite the trial.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant argues that out of total 25 witnesses, 13 have been examined and the applicant continues to languish in jail since 29.10.2017 and is having no criminal history,
may be released on bail.
5. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

6. Considering the fact that the applicant has been for almost six and a half years in jail and there is no likelihood of the trial being completed in the near future, despite directions given on more than one occasion, the right of speedy trial enshrined by virtue of Article 21 of Constitution of India has been adversely affected in the present case.
Thus, on the ground of prolonged pre-trial detention coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
As regards, the applicant is enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant- Pratap Maurya @ Ram Pratap be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
.
[Pankaj Bhatia,J.] Order Date :- 12.3.2024 -Amit K-  
Pratap Maurya @ Ram Pratap vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
